summary: Client-side batch retry causes metadata encoding mismatch during cross-SDK function handoff (Python -> Go)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDocs reports that a resumed batch (client-side retry) originating from their Python service leads to duplicated function executions in a downstream Go microservice. The root cause appears to be metadata key serialization/encoding differences (UTF-8 vs percent-encoding) when the SDK replays batched entries across our gateway, causing the Go SDK to not match the idempotency header and re-execute tool calls.

Impact:
- Several production jobs for BrightDocs experienced duplicate writes to downstream systems; observed 2-3x duplicate side-effects for ~0.4% of batched requests during retry storms.
- Customer on Dedicated tier, high throughput in us-east; business impact reported as lost data consistency for nightly ingestion.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated cluster in us-east-1.
- Python client: redwood-python 0.9.4 (custom wrapper for batch + backoff).
- Go service: redwood-go 1.2.1 receiving function-call webhooks.
- API Gateway: edge sidecar proxies perform header normalization.
- Model used: gptj-6b-quant pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Customer sends a batched request of 50 function calls using python sdk with per-item idempotency tokens (session-scoped prefix + index).
2) During an induced network blip, the python client retries the batch with their custom replay logic (resending the same idempotency keys in a single HTTP request).
3) The edge proxy performs header folding and percent-encodes non-ASCII bytes in idempotency metadata.
4) The Go webhook receiver sees a mismatch between the decoded idempotency key and its stored canonical key and proceeds to re-run the function call.

Observed logs (customer snippets):
- python client: "Resending batch, idempotency_keys=["session:Δ:0001", "session:Δ:0002"]"
- gateway: "normalized-idempotency: session%3A%CE%94%3A0001"
- go webhook: "idempotency lookup miss for key 'session:Δ:0001' - executing function"

Why this is not covered in existing guidance:
- Existing idempotency guidance assumes byte-for-byte preservation of key strings across the transport. This case shows intermediate proxies/SDKs can apply different normalization/encoding rules when replaying batches, especially for non-ASCII characters.

Requested outcome:
- Customer wants a short-term mitigation and a long-term fix so retries do not cause duplicate side-effects across language boundaries.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Arielle): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and requesting request/response capture and proxy logs from customer. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-10 11:03 - CS (Sam): Received pcap and gateway header logs from BrightDocs. Reproduced a key encoding difference in a local staging proxy with percent-encoding enabled.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Eng (Samir): Hypothesis: edge sidecar is applying URL-encoding to header values when it encounters non-ASCII. Go SDK assumes UTF-8 canonicalization. Filed INT-4421 to track a runtime fix.
2026-03-11 12:22 - Customer (Elena, BrightDocs): We've confirmed duplicate writes over last midnight run. Can you advise immediate workaround while you investigate?

2026-03-12 10:15 - Support (Arielle): Suggested customer-side workaround: normalize idempotency tokens to ASCII-safe format (base64url or hex) before sending and avoid non-ASCII in tokens. Customer to test for next run.

2026-03-13 16:02 - Eng (Samir): Put a short-term mitigation in gateway: do not percent-encode known idempotency header keys; added logging for any normalized headers. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428
investigation_notes: Confirmed that python sdk sends raw UTF-8 tokens which included multibyte char U+0394 (Greek Delta) in customer session prefix.
Local repro: replaying a 10-entry batch through dev-proxy with percent-encoding enabled produced header values that differ string-wise when Go receiver decodes vs when Python sent them.
Edge case: HTTP/2 header compression and subsequent proxying steps can transform header bytes; some proxies apply URL-encoding to ensure ASCII-only headers.
Risk assessment: any customer-generated idempotency tokens containing non-ASCII run risk of false misses during replay; likelihood medium-low but high impact for misprocessed batches.
Related INT ticket created to coordinate runtime fix and SDK compatibility tests: INT-4421. See unit tests added in PR 1428 showing round-trip preservation with ascii-safe tokens.
Kept sample logs and pcap in secure customer folder: link in internal ticket (redwood vault).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: advised BrightDocs to adopt ASCII-safe idempotency tokens (base64url of SHA256(session + index)) and to disable any custom client-side replay that modifies header encodings. Engineering applied a gateway patch to bypass percent-encoding for headers named 'x-idempotency-key' and added defensive decoding in Go SDK. Long-term plan: introduce a canonical header encoding contract and add SDK helpers to normalize/derive safe idempotency keys automatically. Scheduled follow-up: roll gateway patch to all dedicated clusters after staged canary (INT-4421). Customer accepted temporary workaround and saw no duplicates on the next nightly run.
next_steps: 1) Complete INT-4421: add round-trip integration tests across python/go/sdk and proxy layer (owner: Samir)
2) Add SDK helper functions in python/go to normalize idempotency tokens (owner: DX team)
3) Publish short KB article outlining safe token formats and examples for multi-lang integrations (owner: Support)
4) Postmortem scheduled after full rollout to capture telemetry and prevent recurrence (owner: SRE)
